members.name: alias
members.description: Stores a generated placeholder value for the user's alias. The placeholder value is `alias`.

members.name: email
members.description: Stores a generated placeholder value for the user's email address. The placeholder value is `placeholder-email@example.com`.

members.name: emailEncodingKey
members.description: Stores the default value for the email encoding type for the user, such as `UTF-8`. The email encoding type determines how Salesforce encodes characters in outgoing emails. The default value is the email encoding key for the execution user specified in the Run As field in the authentication provider definition.

members.name: firstName
members.description: Stores a generated placeholder value for the user's first name. The placeholder value is `placeholder-first-name`.

members.name: languageLocaleKey
members.description: Stores the default value for the user's language, such as `en_US` for English. The default value is the language for the registration handler execution user. The execution user is specified in the Run As field in the authentication provider definition.

members.name: lastName
members.description: Stores a generated placeholder value for the user's last name, also known as family name. The placeholder value is `placeholder-last-name`.

members.name: localesIdKey
members.description: Stores the default value for the user's locale, defined using two-letter International Organization for Standardization (ISO) codes. For example, `en_US` indicates English (United States). The default value is the language for the registration handler execution user. The execution user is specified in the Run As field in the authentication provider definition.

members.name: timeZoneSidKey
members.description: Stores the default value for the user's time zone, such as `(GMT-07:00) Pacific Daylight Time (America/Los_Angeles)`. The time zone is defined using region and key city according to ISO standards. The default value is the time zone for the registration handler execution user. The execution user is specified in the Run As field in the authentication provider definition.

members.name: username
members.description: Stores a generated placeholder value for the user's username. The placeholder value is `placeholder-username<unique 14-character number>@example com`, such as `placeholder-username17370000000000@example com`.

members.description: Returns the not before (`nbf`) claim that identifies the time before which the JWT must not be accepted for processing, while allowing some leeway for clock skew. This method returns a `NoAccess` exception for JWTs generated using methods in the `Auth.JWTUtil` class. To return the `nbf` claim for these JWTs, use the `getAdditionalClaims` method instead.

members.name: getSub

members.name: getValidityLength
members.description: Returns the length of time (in seconds) that the JWT is valid, which affects the expiration (`exp`) claim. This method returns a `NoAccess` exception for JWTs generated using methods in the `Auth.JWTUtil` class. To return the validity length for these JWTs, use the `getAdditionalClaims` method instead.

members.name: setAdditionalClaims
members.description: Sets the additional claims in the JWT. Returned by the `getAdditionalClaims` method.

members.name: setNbfClockSkew

members.name: setSub
members.description: Sets the subject (`sub`) claim in the JWT. Returned by the `getSub` method.

members.name: setValidityLength
members.description: Sets the length of time (in seconds) that the JWT is valid, which affects the expiration (`exp`) claim. Returned by the `getValidityLength` method. This method returns a `NoAccess` exception for JWTs generated using methods in the `Auth.JWTUtil` class. For these JWTs, the incoming JWT determines the validity length.

members.name: moveAfterJob
members.description: Moves the job with the ID jobToMoveId immediately after the job with the ID jobInQueueId in the flex queue. You can move jobToMoveId forward or backward in the queue. If either job isn’t in the queue, it throws an element-not-found exception. Returns `true` if the job is moved, or `false` if jobToMoveId is already immediately after jobInQueueId, so no change is made.

members.name: moveBeforeJob
members.description: Moves the job with the ID jobToMoveId immediately before the job with the ID jobInQueueId in the flex queue. You can move jobToMoveId forward or backward in the queue. If either job isn’t in the queue, it throws an element-not-found exception. Returns `true` if the job is moved, or `false` if jobToMoveId is already immediately before jobInQueueId, so no change is made.

members.name: moveJobToEnd
members.description: Moves the specified job the end of the flex queue, to index position `(size - 1)`. All jobs after the job’s starting position move one spot forward. If the job isn’t in the queue, it throws an element-not-found exception. Returns `true` if the job is moved, or `false` if the job is already at the end of the queue, so no change is made.

members.name: moveJobToFront
members.description: Moves the specified job to the front of the flex queue, to index position `0`. All other jobs move back one spot. If the job isn’t in the queue, it throws an element-not-found exception. Returns `true` if the job is moved, or `false` if the job is already at the front of the queue, so no change is made.

examples.heading: Example
examples.snippet: This example moves a job to the front of the flex queue so that it’s executed immediately. The job is moved by calling the `System.FlexQueue.moveJobToFront()` method with the high priority job ID as the parameter.

members.name: find
members.description: Attempts to find the next subsequence of the input sequence that matches the pattern. This method returns true if a subsequence of the input sequence matches this Matcher object's pattern.

members.name: group
members.description: Returns the input subsequence returned by the previous match.

members.name: group
members.description: Returns the input subsequence captured by the specified group index during the previous match operation. If the match was successful but the specified group failed to match any part of the input sequence, `null` is returned.

members.name: groupCount
members.description: Returns the number of capturing groups in this Matching object's pattern. Group zero denotes the entire pattern and is not included in this count.

members.name: hasAnchoringBounds
members.description: Returns true if the Matcher object has anchoring bounds, false otherwise. By default, a Matcher object uses anchoring bounds regions.

members.name: hasTransparentBounds
members.description: Returns true if the Matcher object has transparent bounds, false if it uses opaque bounds. By default, a Matcher object uses opaque region boundaries.

members.name: hitEnd
members.description: Returns true if the end of input was found by the search engine in the last match operation performed by this Matcher object. When this method returns true, it is possible that more input would have changed the result of the last search.

members.name: lookingAt
members.description: Attempts to match the input sequence, starting at the beginning of the region, against the pattern.

members.name: matches
members.description: Attempts to match the entire region against the pattern.

members.name: pattern
members.description: Returns the Pattern object from which this Matcher object was created.

members.name: quoteReplacement
members.description: Returns a literal replacement string for the specified string inputString. The characters in the returned string match the sequence of characters in inputString.

members.name: region
members.description: Sets the limits of this Matcher object's region. The region is the part of the input sequence that is searched to find a match.

members.name: regionEnd
members.description: Returns the end index (exclusive) of this Matcher object's region.

members.name: regionStart
members.description: Returns the start index (inclusive) of this Matcher object's region.

members.name: replaceAll
members.description: Replaces every subsequence of the input sequence that matches the pattern with the replacement string.

members.name: replaceFirst
members.description: Replaces the first subsequence of the input sequence that matches the pattern with the replacement string.

members.name: requireEnd
members.description: Returns true if more input could change a positive match into a negative one.

members.name: reset
members.description: Resets this Matcher object. Resetting a Matcher object discards all of its explicit state information.

members.name: reset
members.description: Resets this Matcher object with the new input sequence. Resetting a Matcher object discards all of its explicit state information.

members.name: start
members.description: Returns the start index of the first character of the previous match.

members.name: start
members.description: Returns the start index of the subsequence captured by the group specified by the group index during the previous match operation. Captured groups are indexed from left to right, starting at one. Group zero denotes the entire pattern, so the expression `m.start(0)` is equivalent to `m.start()`.

members.name: useAnchoringBounds
members.description: Sets the anchoring bounds of the region for the Matcher object. By default, a Matcher object uses anchoring bounds regions.

members.name: usePattern
members.description: Changes the Pattern object that the Matcher object uses to find matches. This method causes the Matcher object to lose information about the groups of the last match that occurred. The Matcher object's position in the input is maintained.

members.name: useTransparentBounds
members.description: Sets the transparency bounds for this Matcher object. By default, a Matcher object uses anchoring bounds regions.

members.name: compile
members.description: Compiles the regular expression into a Pattern object.

members.name: matcher
members.description: Creates a Matcher object that matches the input string stringtoMatch against this Pattern object.

members.name: matches
members.description: Compiles the regular expression regExp and tries to match it against the specified string. This method returns `true` if the specified string matches the regular expression, `false` otherwise.

members.name: pattern

members.name: quote
members.description: Returns a string that can be used to create a pattern that matches the string yourString as if it were a literal pattern.

members.name: split
members.description: Returns a list that contains each substring of the String that matches this pattern.

members.name: split
members.description: Returns a list that contains each substring of the String that is terminated either by the regular expression regExp that matches this pattern, or by the end of the String.

members.name: getRandomInteger

members.name: getRandomLong

members.name: signXML

members.name: verify

members.name: verify
members.description: Verifies the digital signature for the data blob using the specified algorithm and the supplied public key. Use this method to verify a blob signed by a digital signature created using a third-party application or the sign method.

members.name: verifyHMac
members.description: Verifies the HMAC signature for the data blob using the specified algorithm, input data, private key, and the mac. Use this method to verify a blob signed by a digital signature created using a third-party application or the sign method.

If no HTTPS custom URLs exist in the site, then this method returns

members.name: getBaseUrl

members.name: Delete
members.description: The `delete` DML operation deletes one or more existing sObject records, such as individual accounts or contacts, from your organization’s data. `delete` is analogous to the `delete()` statement in the SOAP API.

members.name: Insert
members.description: The `insert` DML operation adds one or more sObjects, such as individual accounts or contacts, to your organization’s data. `insert` is analogous to the INSERT statement in SQL.

members.name: Merge
members.description: The `merge` statement merges up to three records of the same sObject type into one of the records, deleting the others, and re-parenting any related records.

members.name: Undelete
members.description: The `undelete` DML operation restores one or more existing sObject records, such as individual accounts or contacts, from your organization’s Recycle Bin. `undelete` is analogous to the UNDELETE statement in SQL.

members.name: Update
members.description: The `update` DML operation modifies one or more existing sObject records, such as individual accounts or contacts, in your organization’s data. `update` is analogous to the UPDATE statement in SQL.

members.name: Upsert
members.description: The `upsert` DML operation creates new records and updates sObject records within a single statement, using a specified field to determine the presence of existing objects, or the ID field if no field is specified.

members.description: Returns `true` if the field can be included in the `GROUP BY` clause of a SOQL query, `false` otherwise. This method is only available for Apex classes and triggers saved using API version 18.0 and higher.

members.name: isHtmlFormatted
members.description: Returns `true` if the field has been formatted for HTML and should be encoded for display in HTML, `false` otherwise. One example of a field that returns `true` for this method is a hyperlink custom formula field. Another example is a custom formula field that has an `IMAGE` text function.

members.name: isIdLookup
members.description: Returns `true` if the field can be used to specify a record in an `upsert` method, `false` otherwise.

members.name: isNameField
members.description: Returns `true` if the field is a name field, `false` otherwise.

members.name: isNamePointing
members.description: Returns `true` if the field can have multiple types of objects as parents. For example, a task can have both the Contact/Lead ID (`WhoId`) field and the Opportunity/Account ID (`WhatId`) field return `true` for this method. because either of those objects can be the parent of a particular task record. This method returns `false` otherwise.

members.name: isNillable
members.description: Returns `true` if the field is nillable, `false` otherwise. A nillable field can have empty content. A non-nillable field must have a value for the object to be created or saved.

members.name: isPermissionable
members.description: Returns `true` if field permissions can be specified for the field, `false` otherwise.

members.name: isRestrictedDelete
members.description: Returns `true` if the parent object can't be deleted because it is referenced by a child object, `false` otherwise.

members.name: isRestrictedPicklist
members.description: Returns `true` if the field is a restricted picklist, `false` otherwise

members.name: isSearchPrefilterable
members.description: Returns `true` if a foreign key can be included in prefiltering when used in a SOSL `WHERE` clause, `false` otherwise.

members.name: isSortable
members.description: Returns `true` if a query can sort on the field, `false` otherwise

members.name: isUnique
members.description: Returns `true` if the value for the field must be unique, `false` otherwise

members.name: isUpdateable
members.description: Returns `true` if the field can be edited by the current user, or child records in a master-detail relationship field on a custom object can be reparented to different parent records; `false` otherwise.

members.name: isWriteRequiresMasterRead
members.description: Returns `true` if writing to the detail object requires read sharing instead of read/write sharing of the parent.
